newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria, Romania pledge to fight border crime.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, Romania pledge to fight border crime.

text.p: Bulgaria's president Petar Stoyanov and his Romanian counterpart Emil Constantinescu pledged on Wednesday to combine efforts in fighting cross-border crime, hoping to boost their chances of entering the EU and NATO.
"We discussed our strategic will to join the EU and NATO and the reforms which both countries need to undertake to fulfil this wish," Stoyanov told a joint news conference.
Constantinescu arrived on a half-day visit to Sofia to discuss regional cooperation and bilateral links. Both countries have association agreements with the EU.

The reformist presidents agreed that the fight against corruption, drug smuggling and money laundering was crucial for the success of market reforms in the two Balkan states, lagging behind many of their neighbours in restructuring their economies.
"We have the same goals and the same means to achieve them. These are democratic parliamentary societies and have the will to reform," said Constantinescu, speaking through an interpreter.

Bulgaria and Romania are among several countries lobbying for inclusion in NATO's first eastward expansion to be announced at a summit in Madrid in July. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are seen as more certain candidates.

"Joining our efforts to speed up economic restructuring in the region, fight corruption, and instil confidence that things will change fundamentally, will bring us a step closer to EU and NATO," said Constantinescu.
The two countries vowed once again to renew talks on a new $400 million bridge over the Danube river after years of disagreements over its location.

The new bridge is expected to ease Europe's access to the east as part of the European Union's trans-European network. Bulgaria and Romania are now connected by only one congested bridge and operate two ferry links across the Danube.

"If we had cleared all issues related to the bridge, we would have told you when we are going to cut the ribbon," said Stoyanov after a slip of the tongue in which he confused Constantinescu's name with that of Romanian dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, ousted and shot in December 1989.
Constantinescu is expected to depart for Bucharest later on Wednesday.
